definitions.explanation: Describes something that is certain to occur as a natural or logical consequence. Implies that the outcome could not have been otherwise given the circumstances.

examples.japanese: それは{必然的|ひつぜんてき}な{結果|けっか}だった。
{技術|ぎじゅつ}の{進歩|しんぽ}に{伴|ともな}い、{変化|へんか}は{必然的|ひつぜんてき}に{起|お}こる。
examples.english: With advances in technology, change inevitably occurs.

examples.japanese: {人口|じんこう}が{減|へ}れば、{労働力|ろうどうりょく}{不足|ぶそく}は{必然的|ひつぜんてき}に{深刻|しんこく}になる。
examples.english: If the population declines, the labor shortage will inevitably become severe.

notes: Used both as a な-adjective ({必然的|ひつぜんてき}な{結果|けっか}) and as an adverb with に ({必然的|ひつぜんてき}に). The opposite is {偶然的|ぐうぜんてき} (accidental, coincidental). The base noun {必然|ひつぜん} (inevitability) also stands alone. Common in academic writing, essays, and formal discussion.
